macro.headline: Indexes drift below 50-day with defensive/energy leadership; tape is transitional, not directional.
macro.story:
The facts first: SPY sits at $742.09, down 0.95% over five sessions and below its 50-day moving average with a negative MACD histogram, though still above its 200-day and roughly 7% above that longer-term line. QQQ is weaker (-2.2% over 5d, RSI 42.4, below its 50-day), while the Dow (+0.67% over 21d) and Russell 2000 hold above both moving averages — small caps and cyclicals are outperforming mega-cap growth. VIX is 17.74, up 7.5% in five days, VIX3M sits at 20.54 (contango holding), the 10-year yield is 4.60% (up 3% over 21d) and the DXY is grinding higher at 101.0. WTI crude has run to $83.84 (+9.5% in 21d) while gold, silver and natgas are all still below their 50-day averages. Sector breadth is split: 7 of 11 GICS sectors above their 50-day, Energy and Financials HOT with strong RSI, while Technology, Nasdaq-100, Materials and Consumer Discretionary all sit BEARISH with sub-46 RSI.

The prevailing sentiment attributes this internal rotation to a stack of macro cross-currents rather than any single catalyst. The tracked conversation is split — leaning modestly bullish overall, but with a clear bearish undercurrent on mega-cap growth (NASDAQ, GOOGL, AMZN, NVDA, SPY, TSLA). The dominant explanatory threads are: an escalating Iran conflict driving Brent above $91 (the chart reads point to a decisive break of the $91.20 resistance), fresh 10% tariff headlines on 'dozens of countries', stress showing up in CLO equity returns (worst quarterly print since the 2020 crash per a highlighted chart), and a generational AI-driven displacement in junior software developer employment. Bullish voices are congregating in small-caps (RUT), AI-adjacent infrastructure (NBIS, IREN, CRWV, LITE, AVGO) and idiosyncratic consumer names (HOG). This is broadly consistent with the price data — crude strength + defensive/energy leadership + growth softness all line up with the crude-shock + tariff narrative — though the AI-infrastructure bullish thread partially conflicts with Technology sector momentum registering BEARISH today; the narrative may be running ahead of the tape there.

Rotation-wise, the validated Early-Runway signal is pointing to Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (top-decile RS, roughly halfway through its typical hot spell, +5.4% since the signal fired), Diagnostics & Research, Staffing & Employment Services, REIT-Industrial, Software-Application and Credit Services — a mix of energy, defensives and select cyclicals. That is a genuine, cross-validated tailwind for hunting longs inside those pockets. Meanwhile the DXY-up / metals-below-50-day setup is the validated inverse commodity headwind: gold and silver are trying intraday bounces but the multi-week trend remains DOWN with both below their 200-day.

Forward watch: (1) can SPY reclaim its 50-day and flip MACD, or does the -0.74 histogram deepen into a real breakdown; (2) VIX behaviour around 20 — a hold below keeps the tape orderly, a break above accelerates de-risking; (3) whether Energy's HOT reading extends on further crude strength or fades if the Iran-risk premium unwinds (the active-themes data flags a possible Hormuz-reopening scenario as a risk-on setup, though live sentiment is still trading the escalation side).

This is unambiguously RISK-ON for equities: lower crude reduces input-cost and inflation-expectation pressure, eases the case for further Fed tightening, and removes the dominant macro tail-risk from the narrative. The correct read on oil weakness here is NOT 'Iran re-escalation risk' — it is the OPPOSITE: the Hormuz corridor is reopening and supply constraints are lifting. Energy equities (XLE, E&P names) face near-term margin compression from lower realized prices, but the broader equity market benefits. Transports and consumer discretionary are direct fuel-cost beneficiaries.

**[THE SPINE]** Semiconductor exhaustion is the dominant force this week — the AI infrastructure trade that has carried the tape is hitting its first real air pocket. Semis are HOT for 13 months with a +258% run, the largest on record for this industry, and the group just printed -19.3% over 21 days while still tagged HOLDING_BULLISH. That's the classic ceiling-territory unwind: leadership hasn't broken, but the fuel gauge is empty and the rotation underneath is already telling.

**[CROSS-ASSET LENS]** The macro backdrop is CHOPPY / RISK-ON at 6/10 confidence, with SPY flat (+0.4% on 21d, RSI 47.9, sitting right at the 50SMA) — no trend fade edge here, just a coil. VIX at 17.9 with term structure in contango is not sounding alarms, but VIX is up 8.8% on the month and the whole curve across 2s/5s/10s has pushed higher (10Y at 4.61%, RSI 60, +3.5% on 21d). Per the backtest, the 10Y ceiling call DOESN'T HOLD — yields tend to keep rising after these tags 53% of the time — so treat this as a live rates trend, not a reversal setup. DXY at 101 is mixed vs its SMAs (signal HOLDS but no directional call), and with Gold -3.8% and Silver -10.7% on 21d, the metals complex is already reflecting that dollar posture; the Precious Metals theme is officially FADING.

**[CROSS-ASSET LENS cont.]** Oil is the quiet macro variable — WTI +10% on 21d, RSI 61, and per the backtest there's no mean-reversion edge (trend only). Copper +2.5% and BB above upper adds to the cyclical-inflation whisper. This combination — rising yields, firmer oil/copper, weak metals — argues the reflation/cyclical rotation is real, which is exactly what the sector tape is showing.

**[SECTOR & ROTATION LENS]** Money is leaving the AI-compute complex and rotating into old-economy cyclicals and defensives. XLE leads at +6.8% (21d), XLV +6.1%, XLF +4.0%, XLRE +3.8% — while XLY sits at -0.6% and XLC just +1.7%. Rotation flows show Consumer Electronics, Software - Infrastructure, and one unmapped bucket taking inflows; nothing yet flipping out, but the leadership map has clearly broadened away from mega-cap semis. Regional Banks are choppy but positive (+6% on the current spell); REIT - Retail is running +10% on a 5-month spell that's now above typical.

**[WHERE THE OPPORTUNITY IS]** Semis are ceiling territory — manage exits, don't chase entries. The in-range setups with smart flow are AAPL (Consumer Electronics, BULLISH flow, coil 98%) and TFC (Banks - Regional, BULLISH flow, coil 72.5%) — both sub-10% moves on 5d and 21d, both un-run. Software - Infrastructure is 1 month into a new hot spell with only +3% booked vs +18% typical — early innings, real runway. Internet Content & Info and Software - Application are similar: 1-month spells, gains still below typical, room to work. Avoid piling into names that already printed the 258% move; the pond to fish is the freshly-hot groups where the tape hasn't paid out yet.

**[WHAT TO WATCH]** The tripwire is SPY 739.51 support against the AI complex. If semis keep bleeding and SPY loses 739 with VIX cracking through 18.91 resistance, the rotation becomes a de-risking event and the un-run cyclicals get sold with everything else. Hold 739 with breadth staying above 60% and this is a healthy handoff from semis to broader cyclicals — the bullish case. Also watch 10Y at 4.618 res: a clean break with DXY firming would put fresh pressure on metals and long-duration growth simultaneously.
